title: LLMs Are Not (Consistently) Bayesian: Quantifying Internal (In)consistencies of LLMs’ Probabilistic Beliefs
gist: Apple/Stanford researchers measure an 'information processing gap' — how far LLM belief updates deviate from exact Bayesian updating — and find that non-Bayesian heuristic updates often beat mathematically optimal Bayesian updates on downstream task performance, implying LLMs' internal world models are misspecified.

insights.claim: AI systems now deployed in high-stakes domains like medicine, science, and law often face questions with no single correct answer given the evidence, so they must be able to represent and update uncertain beliefs as new evidence arrives in order to make rational decisions.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Frames belief-calibration, not just factual accuracy, as a prerequisite for deploying LLMs in regulated, high-stakes verticals — relevant to AI-in-healthcare and AI-in-legal-tech investment theses.
insights.locator: Modern AI systems are being deployed in complex domains

insights.claim: The researchers introduce a technique of studying LLMs as information processing rules and define an 'information processing gap' — the deviation from exact Bayesian updates — as a way to quantify internal inconsistencies in how LLMs update their probabilistic beliefs from evidence.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Introduces a reusable metric (the information processing gap) that could become a standard diagnostic for auditing reliability of any LLM-based decision or inference system.
insights.quote: we introduce the novel technique of studying LLMs as information processing rules and utilize the information processing gap—the deviation from Bayes updates—to study the internal (in)consistencies of how LLMs update their probabilistic beliefs from evidence

insights.claim: Across multiple tested approaches for how LLMs incorporate new evidence into beliefs, some approaches produce near-exact Bayesian updates (optimal information processing), while others rely on a learned heuristic instead.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Confirms LLMs do not use one uniform mechanism for belief updating — the method used (exact vs. heuristic) varies by approach, a variable builders should control for when picking prompting/fine-tuning strategies.
insights.quote: Some of these approaches produce (nearly) Bayesian updates, thus optimally processing evidence; others use a learned heuristic.
insights.locator: Our extensive experiments evaluate multiple approaches

insights.claim: Non-Bayesian heuristic belief updates in LLMs often outperform mathematically exact Bayesian updates on downstream task performance, which the researchers say indicates the LLMs' internal probabilistic models of the world are misspecified.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A counterintuitive result: forcing an LLM to be 'more mathematically rigorous' (exact Bayesian updating) can hurt real-world performance when its underlying world model is wrong — a caution against over-engineering formal-correctness constraints into production AI systems without first fixing the underlying model's assumptions.
insights.quote: the non-Bayesian heuristic updates often outperform exact Bayesian updates (optimal information processing) in terms of downstream task performance—indicating the LLMs’ probabilistic models of the world are misspecified

insights.claim: The authors' proposed information-processing-gap measure can serve as a diagnostic tool to identify problems in LLM-powered inferential systems.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Positions the metric as a potential audit/monitoring tool for enterprises deploying LLMs in inference-heavy pipelines (e.g., risk scoring, diagnosis support).
insights.quote: we show how our measure can provide diagnostics to identify issues with LLM-powered inferential systems
insights.locator: Lastly, we show how our measure

insights.claim: A related October 2024 EMNLP paper found that as LLMs are updated across versions to improve aggregate performance metrics, developers often pay less attention to preserving compatibility with earlier versions, causing instance-level regressions where individual cases that used to work correctly start failing, which disrupts users' mental model of the model.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Flags an underappreciated production risk for anyone building on top of frequently-updated LLM APIs: aggregate benchmark improvements can mask silent regressions on specific use cases, so version upgrades need instance-level regression testing, not just headline-metric comparison.
insights.quote: developers often prioritize improving overall performance metrics, paying less attention to maintaining compatibility with earlier model versions
